analyzed_vuln.description: Heap-use-after-free during shutdown is caused by delayed secure-channel cleanup operating on a channel entry that has already been freed. `removeSecureChannel()` enqueues `removeSecureChannelCallback(server, entry)` with raw `channel_list_entry*`. Later, `processDelayedCallbacks()` executes the callback and then unconditionally `UA_free(dc)` for the delayed-callback node. In this PoV, the same underlying channel/session state is cleaned up earlier in shutdown, so `removeSecureChannelCallback` dereferences/frees stale `entry` and calls `UA_SecureChannel_deleteMembersCleanup(&centry->channel)` on freed memory (crash at ua_securechannel.c:105). Root cause is unsafe lifetime management in delayed callback scheduling/ownership for `entry` in secure-channel manager.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger requires binary message sequence that creates a session/secure channel, then causes channel removal to be scheduled via `UA_Server_delayedCallback` (from `removeSecureChannel`) and server shutdown (`UA_Server_run_shutdown`) to process delayed callbacks. If the `channel_list_entry` is already freed/cleaned by prior shutdown path before delayed callback runs, callback uses dangling pointer, leading to UAF when iterating `channel->sessions` in `UA_SecureChannel_deleteMembersCleanup`.
